text.p: On overnight commodity markets, aluminium prices sunk to a two-and-a-half year low on the London Metals Exchange as speculative selling knocked out a key support level.
Copper prices also sank, but to a lesser extent. Gold prices rose in Comex trade, helped by a rumour that Russian President Boris Yeltsin had died. The rumour was later denied.
Wheat prices ended mostly higher in Chicago overnight on concerns about delays to the seeding of the U.S. crop.
Oil prices fell in sympathy with a slump in U.S. heating oil prices after heating oil stocks rose. Sugar prices in New York ended a touch weaker in range trade.
METALS
Aluminium spun lower during Wednesday LME trading, as the market came under persistent speculative selling pressure which knocked away potential support levels, traders said.
Elsewhere in a distinctly off-colour metals complex there were losses seen in copper as Tuesday's upside enthusiasm evaporated, and a setback in nickel values.

Aluminium was knocked off its stride by commission house sales and liquidation, which resulted in previous lows and the important $1,330 level giving way. The tide was halted just below $1,320, with prices bottoming at $1,316, but the market seems destined to head under $1,300 soon. Last kerb trade today was at $1,323 a tonne, down $23.50 from
Tuesday's kerb close. Copper turned lower once the early attempt to run the market above $1,950 and re-challenge of $1,970 faltered.

Last business was at $1,928, down $21 from yesterday, with a well-defined $1,900/10 to $1,950/70 range available for the market to fluctuate in short-term. Nickel prices stabilised during slow afternoon trading, after liquidation at midsession sent the market into a tail-spin from near the $7,200 level.
Last trade was at $7,130 a tonne, down $120 from yesterday. GOLD
New York precious metals futures ended mostly higher, led by gains in silver, and helped by a rumor, later denied by officials, that Russian president Yeltsin had died, traders said.
"Precious metals month-long downtrend looks to have ended for now, but sideways looks to be the most likely direction from here," Mitsui USA bullion dealer Greg Drury said.

"Above the market there is central bank and producer selling, with the $385.00 level important for producer hedging, while below the market is good physical demand, so I wouldn't be a believer unless gold climbs over $386," he said.

COMEX December gold ended up 10 cents at $383.50 an ounce, after trading in a $382.60-384.40 range. In New York bullion trade, spot gold ended quoted $381.05/381.55 an ounce, after seeing a session high around $381.90, compared to the London
Wednesday afternoon fix at $381.35 and the New York close Tuesday at $381.10/381.60.
CBOT WHEAT
CBOT wheat futures closed mostly higher, led by deferred months, with support stemming from concerns about delays in seeding portions of the U.S. soft red winter wheat crop, traders said.

Cash dealers early Friday indicated the eastern U.S. growing region would be slow in seeding the wheat crop due to the late harvest of soybeans. The late maturation of the soybean crop in the U.S. eastern Corn Belt led to the talk.
A significant portion of wheat in that area is grown on land also used for soybeans.
The U.S. soybean crop in some areas was planted late this year because of a wet spring seeding season.

USDA Monday confirmed the wheat seeding pace in Ohio, Indiana and Illinois were well behind the year-ago and average pace for this time of year. Some traders also said the market was boosted by delays in harvesting of the Canadian spring wheat crop. Wheat closed 5-1/4 cents a bushel higher to 1-1/2 lower, with December down 1-1/2 at $4.27.
NYMEX OIL
NYMEX heating oil prices ended sharply lower Wednesday after oil inventory data showed a bearish build in distillate stocks and ignited profit-taking. Crude oil prices followed.
"The dam finally broke. People decided to take profits while they can," said Al Lindseth, a trader with GSC Energy. November heat settled off 2.22 cents to 73.97 cents a gallon.

The sell-off in heating oil took crude lower, with November crude oil ending down 47 cents a barrel at $25.07. Selling in crude accelerated late session after U.N. Under-Secretary General Chinmaya Gharekhan said he was trying to get visas for three oil monitors from the Dutch-based Saybolt firm to go to Iraq for the pending Iraqi oil-for-food plan.
But, he also said minimum conditions had still not been met to implement the plan.
SUGAR

CSCE world sugar futures settled slightly weaker in thin and rangebound dealings as the March contract inched towards nearby support seen at 10.70, floor sources said. But volume has remained extremely light as prices have crawled lower. Today's activity was estimated to have reached 12,780 lots. The spot-March contract finished 0.04 lower at 10.78, having ranged from 10.80 to 10.72. The back months closed 0.05 higher to 0.01 lower.
